findings.title: Stateful subclass left abstract and uninstallable
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data). Python ABCs prevent instantiation of such a class, so Detector.detector_handler doing group_type.detector_handler(self) for type metric_alert_fire will raise TypeError instead of returning a handler. process_detectors does not catch this, so any detector of this type crashes processing.

findings.title: get_state_data KeyErrors when counter_names is empty
findings.body: get_state_data initializes counter_updates to {} and only populates it inside if self.counter_names:. The result-building loop unconditionally does counter_updates[gk]. When a detector defines counter_names as an empty list, the dict stays empty and every group key raises KeyError, making empty counter lists unusable.

findings.title: Empty redis pipeline is always executed
findings.body: _bulk_commit_redis_state builds a pipeline then calls pipeline.execute() unconditionally, even when both dedupe_updates and counter_updates are empty. Executing an empty pipeline is a wasted Redis round-trip and on some clients raises an error. It should return early when there is nothing to write.

findings.title: Unsafe DetectorPriorityLevel to PriorityLevel cast
findings.body: evaluate_group_key_value does PriorityLevel(new_status) where new_status is a DetectorPriorityLevel. This assumes the two IntEnums share identical numeric values. If they diverge or a new detector level is added, this raises ValueError at evaluation time and drops detection. An explicit mapping should be used instead of a direct enum cast.

findings.title: None / unexpected result treated as status change
findings.body: create_issue_occurrence_from_result branches only on isinstance(result.result, IssueOccurrence) and treats everything else as a status_change payload. If result.result is None or an unexpected type, it calls produce_occurrence_to_kafka with occurrence=None and status_change=None or an invalid object, which will fail downstream or publish corrupt data. It should explicitly handle StatusChangeMessage and reject None.

findings.title: Fingerprint building assumes string group_key
findings.body: build_fingerprint does ':' + group_key. If a DetectorGroupKey is ever an int or other non-str type, this raises TypeError. An f-string interpolation would handle all key types safely.
